Start with [a first model](../get-started.qmd), then follow
[the complete workflow](golden-path.qmd) from a simulated subject effect to a
group estimate. For real brain data, the [FIAC analysis](real-data-fiac.qmd)
works through two runs of a published experiment.

## Explore through figures

[![Eight axial slices of the FIAC sentence contrast, with a shared t-statistic color scale.](../assets/fiac-sentence-effect.png){fig-alt="Eight axial slices showing positive and negative FIAC same-sentence minus different-sentence t statistics."}](real-data-fiac.qmd)

The FIAC tutorial explains how the design and contrast produce this map.
For smaller examples you can run without a download, try
the [figure gallery](plot-gallery.qmd), [plotting and visualization](plotting-visualization.qmd),
[estimating HRFs](estimating-hrfs.qmd), or
[examining a group model](group-diagnostics.qmd).

## Learn the analysis

| Tutorial | What you will do |
| --- | --- |
| [The complete workflow](golden-path.qmd) | Recover a simulated effect through a first-level fit, contrast, and group model; read a separate parity receipt. |
| [A real FIAC analysis](real-data-fiac.qmd) | Fit two runs, define sentence and speaker contrasts, and reconstruct brain maps. |
| [Workflow overview](overview-workflow.qmd) | See how timing, dataset, specification, fit, and contrast objects connect. |
| [Datasets](datasets.qmd) | Work with feature matrices, spatial images, archives, and chunks. |
| [Design matrices](design-matrices.qmd) | Turn event timing into regressors and inspect their column metadata. |
| [Linear models](linear-model.qmd) | Fit a first-level GLM and check a known face-minus-scene effect. |
| [Contrasts](contrasts.qmd) | Test named conditions, pairwise differences, and omnibus hypotheses. |
| [Group analysis](group-analysis.qmd) | Collect subject estimates and fit group models and meta-regressions. |

## Inspect and extend

| Tutorial | What you will do |
| --- | --- |
| [Figure gallery](plot-gallery.qmd) | Inspect the current design, contrast, fit, HRF, time-course, and residual plot families on one simulated study. |
| [Plotting and visualization](plotting-visualization.qmd) | Compare HRFs, view design heatmaps and correlations, and inspect timing. |
| [Estimate an HRF](estimating-hrfs.qmd) | Fit smooth FIR response curves and inspect uncertainty and smoothing. |
| [Group diagnostics](group-diagnostics.qmd) | Compare subject maps and inspect surprise, influence, and review flags. |
| [Single-trial estimates](single-trial.qmd) | Recover trial amplitudes with labels and standard errors. |
| [Parametric modulators](parametric-modulators.qmd) | Model trial covariates and understand centering and orthogonalization. |
| [Sketched and AR-aware models](sketched-ar-models.qmd) | Compare low-rank estimates and configure temporal autocorrelation. |
| [Robust model pieces](robust-models.qmd) | Inspect how residual scale and weights change a refit. |
| [Functional connectivity](functional-connectivity.qmd) | Extract spatial ROI signals, remove nuisance effects, and estimate associations. |
| [Simulation](simulation.qmd) | Generate BOLD responses and noise for method checks. |
| [Benchmark datasets](benchmark-datasets.qmd) | Fit deterministic fixtures and compare estimates with known coefficients. |
